The instant petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed on behalf of petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no.309/2022 registered at Police Station Madhu Vihar,
Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).
6.
Issue notice.
Mr. Anand V. Khatri, learned ASC accepts notice on behalf of the State.

7. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Arvind Bhardwaj and Investigating Officer (IO) ASI Prabhat Kumar from Police Station Madhu Vihar,
Delhi.

8. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no.1 and respondent No. 2 got married on 30.11.2014 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at U.P. One child namely Tulsi was born on 27.10.2015, out of the said wedlock.
Due to temperamental differences, parties started living separately since 27.11.2017.

sentences.text: On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between them before Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi vide Mediation Settlement dated 07.12.2022 and had obtained decree of divorce from the concerned Court.

10. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the affidavits showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court have been filed and the same are on record.

11. It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

8. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 15,00,000/- in five installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 3 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statement in the first motion petition. b. Second installment of Rs. 3 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of withdrawal of defamation case.

Third installment of Rs. 3 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of withdrawal of complaint under D.V. Act.
d. Fourth installment of Rs. 3 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of second motion petition.
e. Fifth/Final instalment of Rs. 3 Lakhs to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

12. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 3 Lakhs today, i.e., 17.11.2023 vide DD No. 208046 drawn on State Bank of India and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

sentences.text: In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

14. Accordingly, FIR bearing no.309/2022 registered at Police Station Madhu Vihar,
Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of Indian Penal Code,
1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.

15. In view of above, the present petition alongwith pending application, if any,
stands disposed of.
16. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
